rules.title: Security deposit limit: 1 month's rent (general rule)
rules.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month's rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.summary: A landlord may not charge more than one month's rent as a security deposit, in addition to the first month's rent, subject to certain exceptions.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant
rules.exemption_note: Small landlords (natural persons owning ≤2 properties with ≤4 total units) may charge up to 2 months' rent, except for service members. Service members paying higher security due to credit/history must have the excess returned after 6 months if rent is current.
rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of security may subject landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Security deposit limit: 2 months' rent for small landlords
rules.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months' rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements: (i) The landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons. (ii) The landlord owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.summary: Small landlords who are natural persons and own no more than two properties with a total of four or fewer units may charge up to two months' rent as a security deposit, except for service members.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_text: Applies only to landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs where all members are natural persons) owning ≤2 properties with ≤4 total units; does not apply to service members
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply if prospective tenant is a service member; landlord cannot refuse to rent to service member because of this limitation.
rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of security may subject landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Higher security for service members must be refunded after 6 months if rent current
rules.quote: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged. The additional amount of security shall be returned to the tenant after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears for any rent due during that period.
rules.summary: If a landlord charges a service member a higher security deposit due to credit or rental history, the additional amount must be returned after six months if the tenant has paid rent on time.
rules.effective_date_evidence: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property
rules.coverage_text: Applies only to service members charged higher security due to credit history, credit score, housing history, or other tenant-related factor
rules.exemption_note: Applies only to service members as defined in Military and Veterans Code § 400.
rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of security may subject landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Security deposit itemization and return within 21 days
rules.quote: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to the expiration of a fixed-term lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant
rules.summary: Within 21 days after a tenant vacates, the landlord must provide an itemized statement showing how the security deposit was used and return any remaining balance.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant
rules.penalty: Landlord not entitled to claim any amount of security if landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply; bad faith may subject landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the security amount, plus actual damages.

rules.title: Photographs required before and after tenancy
rules.quote: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy. Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.summary: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs at move-in; starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs after move-out before and after repairs for which they deduct from the deposit.
rules.effective_date_evidence: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy. Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned
rules.coverage_text: Move-in photos required for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025; move-out photos required beginning April 1, 2025
rules.exemption_note: Move-in photo requirement applies only to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025; move-out photo requirement applies to all tenancies beginning April 1, 2025.

rules.title: Documentation of deductions required with itemized statement
rules.quote: The landlord shall also include, along with and at the same time the itemized statement is sent, copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, as follows: (A) If the landlord or landlord's employee did the work, the itemized statement shall reasonably describe the work performed. The itemized statement shall include the time spent and the reasonable hourly rate charged. (B) If the landlord or landlord's employee did not do the work, the landlord shall provide the tenant a copy of the bill, invoice, or receipt supplied by the person or entity performing the work.
rules.summary: Landlords must provide documentation (invoices, receipts, or descriptions of work with time and hourly rate) for all deductions from the security deposit along with the itemized statement.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all security deposit deductions for repairs or cleaning; exemption if deductions ≤$125 or tenant waives documentation
rules.exemption_note: Documentation not required if deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed $125, or if tenant waives the right after notice to terminate is given.
rules.penalty: Landlord not entitled to claim any amount of security if landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply with subdivision (h).
